WHY ABN EXISTS
The Vision Matters. So Do the People Carrying It.

Leadership and organisational growth present different challenges. They deserve focused solutions. That is why ABN is built around two divisions.

A

A pastor may need perspective from someone who understands the responsibilities of ministry.

B

A church may need a better website, clearer messaging, or more dependable production systems.

C

A real estate professional may need a recognisable brand that communicates expertise and builds confidence.

01 · THE ABN NETWORK
For the Person Behind the Leadership.

A private peer community being developed for senior pastors and ministry leaders who value trust, honest conversations and meaningful relationships.

For the Mission Behind the Organisation.

Creative strategy, digital development, marketing and production services that help organisations communicate more effectively.

THE ABN PRIVATE LEADERSHIP NETWORK
You Spend Your Life Being There for Others. Who's There for You?

Leadership often requires difficult decisions, personal sacrifice and the ability to navigate situations few people fully understand.

Even experienced leaders benefit from relationships where they can exchange perspectives without the expectations of their everyday roles. The ABN Network is being developed to create space for those relationships.

WHY THE NETWORK EXISTS
“The most dangerous place for a senior leader is a room full of people who can't tell them the truth.”
Ministry has changed. The infrastructure hasn't kept up.

The demands on senior pastors have grown: organisational complexity, public scrutiny, the pressure of digital ministry, and the emotional weight of shepherding congregations through cultural turbulence.

Most peer structures built for ministry leaders were designed for a different era: conferences with thousands of attendees, denominations that prioritise alignment over honesty, coaching programs that treat every leader the same.

The ABN Network is being built as the other kind of room, where the people across the table carry the same weight and aren't trying to sell you something, impress you or protect their position.

MEMBER EXPERIENCE
What the Network is being built to offer.

Planned elements of membership. Final terms are confirmed with each formal invitation.

01

The Shepherd's Roundtable

A private, invitation-only gathering that meets quarterly, with 8–12 leaders in each session. The first is planned for June 2027.

About the Roundtable
02

Leadership Dinners & Retreats

Curated dinners for 8–12 leaders in select cities, beginning with a planned Atlanta dinner, and an inaugural leadership retreat planned for Q3 2027.

See Experiences
03

Connection Between Gatherings

Relationships that continue beyond individual events. 

04

Ascend Studio for Members

Access to ABN's creative studio for brand, web, media and events. 

COMMUNITY VALUES
Why this room is different from every other room you've been in.
I

No celebrities. No headliners.

No featured speakers at an ABN gathering. No one is brought in to impress the room.

II

Confidentiality is structural.

Nothing posted from inside the room, no one quoted without consent, and no marketing made from what members share.

III

Intentionally small. Always.

Gatherings are sized for real conversation, not to maximise reach. Small is the feature, not the constraint.

IV

Built to compound, not to consume.

The value builds over time, with each gathering, each peer relationship and each honest conversation.

FOUNDING MEMBERSHIP
The first 50 leaders set the standard for everything that follows.

The founding cohort is not a waitlist. It is the first room, and the relationships formed in it will shape the character of ABN for years to come. Formal invitations are planned to begin in February 2027.

Expressions of interest are welcome. Participation is subject to review and formal invitation.

Express Interest
WHO CAN JOIN
Built for leaders who are already leading.

A STRONG FIT

Senior Pastors
Carrying organisational and spiritual leadership at the same time.
Founding Pastors
Building something from scratch while also sustaining it.
Executive Pastors & Ministry Directors
Leading at an organisational level in complex, mission-driven environments.
Ministry Leaders
Carrying significant regional, denominational or parachurch responsibility.

NOT A FIT RIGHT NOW

The Network is not designed for emerging leaders, early-career associate pastors, or anyone looking for a structured curriculum. The room's value depends on everyone in it leading at a similar level.

MEMBERSHIP PROCESS
Four steps. No automated responses.

Every submission is reviewed personally. We respond within 48 hours.

01

Submit a consideration request

Share who you are, your role and what you're navigating.

02

A private 20-minute call

Not an interview: a real exchange about whether this is the right room for this season.

03

A clear answer

Yes or not yet, and why. No automated declines, no form letters.

04

Formal invitation

Founding invitations are planned to begin in February 2027.

Request Membership Consideration
MEMBERSHIP FAQS
Common questions.
Who is the Network designed for?

Senior pastors, founding pastors, executive pastors and ministry leaders carrying significant organisational responsibility. If you're unsure whether you're a fit, the consideration call is the right next step.

How does the invitation process work?
Where do gatherings take place?
What does membership include?
Is ABN connected to a denomination?

A trusted room for the people who lead.

THE NETWORK'S SIGNATURE EXPERIENCE
The Shepherd's Roundtable.

A different room. A deeper conversation. A private, invitation-only gathering for senior pastors and ministry leaders, being developed for honest dialogue that doesn't happen in public.

Request Consideration
The format
Jun '27

Inaugural · planned

Jun '27

INAUGURAL GATHERING · PLANNED

4×

A YEAR · QUARTERLY

8–12

LEADERS PER SESSION

0

SPEAKERS, SPONSORS OR AUDIENCE

Why the Roundtable exists

“The most dangerous place for a senior leader is a room full of people who can't tell them the truth.”

No speakers. No sponsors. No audience. Just leaders who have earned their seats, and the discipline to leave titles at the door.

RULES OF THE ROOM
The structure that earns the trust.
01

No speakers. No experts.

Everyone in the room is a peer. No one presents, and every voice carries equal weight.

02

No public agenda.

What's discussed stays in the room: no social media, no attributed quotes, no marketing made from what is shared.

03

Curated, not open.

Every seat is considered. The value depends on the calibre and compatibility of who sits at the table.

04

Titles stay at the door.

Inside, you are a leader in a room of leaders: a peer doing the same hard work.

THE FORMAT
Four deliberate phases.

Each phase earns the next, taking a room of peers to the conversation that matters.

01

Opening context

A brief framing: a question or theme surfaced from the group ahead of time, to anchor the conversation without controlling it.

02

Open-table conversation

The core of the Roundtable. Leaders talk to each other, not to a facilitator.

03

Closing commitments

Each leader names one decision, question or shift they're taking with them.

04

Follow-through

Connection continues between gatherings. 

THE INAUGURAL GATHERING
June 2027. The first room.

The first Shepherd's Roundtable is planned for June 2027 with the founding cohort of the ABN Network. Founding invitations are planned to begin in February 2027.

Location is shared with invited leaders

Expressions of interest are welcome. Participation is subject to review and formal invitation. We respond within 48 hours.

THE CHALLENGE
Most people meet your church online long before they walk in.

The mission hasn't changed. What has changed is where people first encounter it: a search result, a social post, a livestream on a Tuesday night. If that first impression is unclear, the message never gets the hearing it deserves.

01

A brand that no longer fits

The identity was right for the church you were, not the church you are becoming.

02

A website visitors can't use

Service times, directions and next steps are hard to find on a phone.

03

A message that stops on Sunday

Sermons and stories don't travel through the week to the people who need them.

04

Media your team struggles to run

Cameras, sound and streaming that depend on one volunteer who knows how it works.

Social strategy, content calendars, email, local search and podcast production, so Sunday's message travels all week.

Planning and coordination for conferences, outreach events and launches, with professional video and photography.

Cameras, lighting, sound, LED and streaming, designed, sourced and installed, with training so your team can run it.

services-faq.question: What does a project cost?
services-faq.answer: What does a project cost?Every engagement is custom-scoped; there are no packages or templates. The free strategy call is how we work out what's right for your situation and budget.

services-faq.question: How long does a website take?
services-faq.answer: How long does a website take?It depends on scope and how quickly content is provided. You receive a specific timeline in the proposal.

services-faq.question: Do you work with small churches?
services-faq.answer: Do you work with small churches?Yes: church plants, growing congregations and multi-site ministries. Scope scales to your situation.

services-faq.question: What makes Ascend Studio different?
services-faq.answer: What makes Ascend Studio different?Our founding team brings 7+ years of agency experience in brand, web and marketing for churches, ministries and faith-aligned businesses.

services-faq.question: Do you work outside our city?
services-faq.answer: Do you work outside our city?Yes. Ascend Studio works nationwide. Most engagements run remotely; on-site work such as events and media setup is available.

network-faq.question: Who is the Network designed for?
network-faq.answer: Who is the Network designed for?Senior pastors, founding pastors, executive pastors and ministry leaders carrying significant organisational responsibility. If you're unsure whether you're a fit, the consideration call is the right next step.

network-faq.question: How does the invitation process work?
network-faq.answer: How does the invitation process work?Submit a brief consideration request. We review every submission personally, respond within 48 hours and follow up with a private 20-minute call. After the call you receive a clear answer.

network-faq.question: Where do gatherings take place?
network-faq.answer: Where do gatherings take place?ABN is a nationwide network. Gatherings are planned in major ministry cities across the US. Location details are shared after membership is confirmed.

network-faq.question: What does membership include?
network-faq.answer: What does membership include?The Shepherd's Roundtable (quarterly), curated dinners and retreats, and connection between gatherings.

network-faq.question: Is ABN connected to a denomination?
network-faq.answer: Is ABN connected to a denomination?No. ABN is independent and non-denominational, and designed to serve leaders across the spectrum of faith traditions.
